goal: Ask, for the first time in P21, what the kernel depends on and whether a credential was ever committed into its tree. P21A through P21F each closed a boundary gap inside the kernel's own code; none of them audited the npm or the Python dependency set, and none of them looked for a secret in the tracked tree. This package adds exactly one new blocking, least-privilege .github/workflows/security.yml: it audits the locked npm production set and the hash-locked db environment against pinned tooling, and it scans the current tracked snapshot — extracted outside the checkout, never the Git history — for committed credentials with a digest-pinned scanner whose output is projected down to four non-disclosing fields. The two deliberate embedded-credential negative fixtures in the consumer-sync test are labelled inline so the scan can walk past exactly them and nothing else. Every fixed expectation is owned by the frozen test file; this manifest is a load-bearing gate and supplies no expected value back to any assertion.

conditionalDeliveryGates.evidence: One problem only: the kernel's dependencies were never audited and its tracked tree was never scanned for a committed credential. Every changed line serves that one problem — one workflow, one manifest, one frozen test and two inline labels on two pre-existing known-bad fixture lines. No unrelated refactor, rename, cleanup or CI change rides along, and ci.yml is not touched.

Exactly the four files named in allowedFiles were touched, declared up front and unchanged since: git status shows one new workflow, one new manifest, the untracked frozen test and one modified test file whose diff is two same-line comments and nothing else. No src/** file, no Python file, no manifest of another package and no prior P21 evidence artifact is touched.

The workflow reuses the repository's existing CI shape — the same fork-safe trigger pair, the same top-level read-only permissions block, the same commit-pinned uses: convention and the same runner — rather than inventing a second convention beside it. No scanning, auditing, hashing or reporting logic is written here: npm audit, uv export, pip-audit and the scanner image do the work, each pinned. No new dependency, module, script or checker was added, and no existing checker was duplicated.

No test was weakened, skipped or made conditional; the frozen test was never edited and its sha256 is unchanged from the handoff snapshot. Nothing in the workflow is excused: there is no continue-on-error, no || true, no set +e, no unconditional exit 0, no allow-listed advisory id, no --ignore-vuln, no detector filter, no path filter and no scanner config file. The audit level is fixed at high, the Python export keeps its hashes and pip-audit is forbidden from resolving anything itself. The two inline ignores are a labelling change on two known-bad lines that already existed at this base; they delete nothing and the frozen test proves both fixtures are still present.

discoveryEvidence.method: Each action pin is the commit SHA of the named official GitHub release tag, recorded here beside the tag it resolved from so a later reader can re-derive it from the action's own release list instead of trusting this file. The scanner is pinned by image digest rather than by tag, because a tag is mutable and a digest is the image. The pip-audit version and the exact npm audit invocation are fixed by the frozen test, which is the only oracle for them; this block records them so the pins are re-derivable, never so an assertion can read them back.

scanBoundary.snapshotMechanism: git archive --format=tar HEAD extracted under RUNNER_TEMP, so the scanner sees the tree as it stands with no repository metadata directory and no history beside it
scanBoundary.note: A current-tree scan cannot see a credential that was committed and then removed: it is still in the history, still fetchable by anyone with the repository, and this gate will report nothing about it. It also cannot see a secret that never entered the tree — one held in a CI secret store, a developer machine or a deployment environment. Choosing the current tree is deliberate: it makes the gate fast, deterministic and identical on every pull request, and it never lets a historical finding no one can fix block an unrelated change. Auditing and, where needed, rotating anything already in the history is a separate, explicitly out-of-scope decision, and this package makes no claim about it.

gateContract.triggers: pull_request and push to main only. pull_request_target, schedule, workflow_run, repository_dispatch and merge_group are all absent: a scanner that runs with a more privileged token, or outside the change being reviewed, is a scanner an untrusted pull request can turn into an exfiltration path.
gateContract.privilege: one top-level permissions block granting contents: read and nothing else, no job widening it, no secret referenced and no workflow token named.
gateContract.pinning: every uses: step is pinned to a full 40-hex commit and the scanner to an image digest; no movable tag or branch is used anywhere.
gateContract.blocking: every gate fails the job on a finding. The scanner runs with verification off, reports unverified results and still fails on them, fails on its own scan errors, and its pipeline runs under pipefail so its exit code survives the pipe into jq.
gateContract.redaction: the scanner's output is projected through jq to exactly four non-disclosing fields — detector name, the scanner's own redacted match, file and line. Raw match content is never projected, never printed and never stored: a CI log is a published artifact, and a secret printed into one is a second disclosure on top of the first.
gateContract.sanctionedFindings: exactly two inline ignores exist in the whole tracked tree, both on the same line as a labelled embedded-credential negative fixture in the consumer-sync test — a URL carrying userinfo before the canonical host, which is precisely what that test exists to refuse. No detector, path or config exclusion is used anywhere, because either of those is an invisible blind spot.

residuals: The Git history is unscanned. A credential that was committed and later removed is still fetchable by anyone who can clone the repository, and this gate will never mention it. A one-off historical audit, and any rotation it implies, is a separate owner decision.

The scan is only as good as its detectors. A credential in a shape no detector recognises passes silently, and with verification off the gate cannot tell a live secret from a dead one — it fails on both, which is the safe direction but produces false alarms that a human must read.

The dependency audits see only what the advisory databases already know. A vulnerability published tomorrow in a dependency pinned today passes today and blocks tomorrow; the gate is a moving floor, not a proof of safety.
npm audit covers the production dependency set only, so a compromised development-only dependency is not caught here.
Nothing about runtime secrets is covered: environment variables, deployment configuration and any future CI secret store are outside this gate entirely.
P21 completion: not claimed. P21G closes only the unscanned-dependency and unscanned-tree gap, and no hosted product journey becomes runnable because of it.

userJourney.once: Kernel'in kendi kodu her pakette biraz daha sıkı denetleniyordu ama kimse şunu sormuyordu: bu kod hangi dış paketlerin üzerinde duruyor ve o paketlerin bilinen bir açığı var mı? Bir de kimse ağaca yanlışlıkla bir parola ya da anahtar düşmüş mü diye bakmıyordu. İki soru da hiç sorulmadığı için cevabı da yoktu.
userJourney.simdi: Her pull request ve main'e her push, üç kapıdan geçmek zorunda: npm tarafındaki üretim bağımlılıklarında yüksek ya da kritik bir açık varsa durur, Python tarafındaki kilitli ortam sürüm ve hash'leriyle birlikte denetlenip açık bulunursa durur, ve o anki takip edilen ağaçta gömülü bir kimlik bilgisi bulunursa durur. Bulunan şey CI kaydına açık açık yazılmaz; sadece hangi tür, hangi dosya, hangi satır ve tarayıcının kendi maskelediği hâli görünür.
userJourney.fark: Önce sadece 'bizim kodumuz doğru mu' sorusu vardı; şimdi 'bizim kodumuzun dayandığı şeyler güvenli mi ve ağaca sızmış bir sır var mı' soruları da her değişiklikte otomatik soruluyor. Hiçbir kapı 'bu seferlik geç' diyemiyor: istisna listesi yok, kapatma anahtarı yok, sadece testin bilerek kötü örnek olarak tuttuğu iki satır etiketli.

userJourney.kalanEngel: Bu bir depo kapısıdır, çalışan bir ürün değildir. Geçmiş commit'ler taranmıyor: ağaçtan silinmiş ama geçmişte kalmış bir parola bu kapıya takılmaz. Tarayıcının tanımadığı biçimdeki bir sır da fark edilmez. Seçilmiş bir sunucu, ağ dinleyicisi, gerçek oturum açma ve barındırılan bir kullanıcı yolculuğu hâlâ yok.
